edits.old: No personal data element is declared: the shapes carry identifiers, codes, versions and references.
edits.new:
No personal data element is declared: the shapes carry identifiers, codes, versions and references.

Assumptions settled for the open values (GAP-0636, GAP-0637, GAP-0638, GAP-0639, GAP-0640, GAP-0641): the step is a named member of the promotion_conditions of the version until a decision_code column is agreed, and the approval reference is a named member of the same jsonb, carried as approval_ref and added as a backward-compatible column whose migration number is taken from the rwb-agent Flyway sequence at build time. A version is in force when its status is APPROVED and the run date is inside its window, with one version per step and date. A run is identified by its step and not by an agent code. The unit of change is a policy version, and the per-decision key is carried in RWB-P10-AD020-APP. The autonomy mode accepts only OFF, SHADOW and L1 until LOV-AUTONOMY is extended by its owner; L2 is then governed by the step-up key RWB-P10-E8004. The approved autonomy level is read from the approval subject and never from approval_level, and the approval instant is taken from updated_at and the approver role from rwb-access. The evidence of a change is agent_policy.evaluation_run_id and the breach is an agent_alert row of type DRIFT. The three read resources gain step, autonomyMode, policyVersion and approvalRef; the decision record carries decision_code with recommendation.autonomyMode and recommendation.policyVersion, and the configuration version is named in the rule-version element of the record. At L1 the agent output carries the recommendation marker and no applied-outcome element. The fakes stub the rwb-valuation route as POST /api/recovery/valuation/v1/cases/{caseId}/route. The three operations of the configuration change are GET and POST /admin/agent-configs and POST /admin/agent-configs/{versionId}/approve; the Arch v5 summary label GET and POST /agent-policies is a summary. The authorise call is made through the gateway-bff route. A 404 means the version id is unknown; a 409 means the version is not LOADED or the caller loaded it; a repeat under the same Idempotency-Key returns the first answer. The kind of a configuration resource is POLICY or PROMPT. The approval answer's element names and the file column set are settled at the wave 4 contract freeze.
